note: Both sets cover the same 17 claims and differ only in how the INT. STEP and FINISH FLOOR level values are typed. Set A states each level twice, once as a bare 'height' (a misbinding, since 2'-6 1/8" and 2'-0 3/8" are level/elevation markers in the datum stack GROUND PLANE 0" … CEILING FINISH 10'-0 1/2") and once as an elevation with the datum condition. Set B types them as 'height above ground plane', keeping the condition and the correct property, and only its two plain 'elevation' claims drop the datum condition. Both sets duplicate these facts and both omit CEILING FINISH 10'-0 1/2".
remarks: Both sets miss CEILING FINISH 10'-0 1/2", the fourth level marker in the same datum stack, which is the main engineering fact left out. Both bind keynote/spec codes (22 11 16, 11 31 13.A7) to a generic 'Water Supply System' and give 'location' values like 'right side of enclosure' / 'indicated by leader line' that are layout trivia rather than engineering content; these are identical in both sets so they do not affect the comparison. The image is legible; the text layer is a flat dump with no positional data, so leader-line/position claims cannot be verified from the text alone.
